77115 The claimant’s household may include


1. the claimant


2. the claimant’s partner


3. any additional spouse in a polygamous marriage case.

relatives.

Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"Temporary residence in a care home

Claimants who have no partner
78084 An additional amount for the severely disabled may not be applicable if a claimant who has no

partner does not normally live alone1. Such a claimant will not satisfy the conditions for this additional
amount while they are temporarily in a care home (see DMG 77007). This is because their stay is
temporary and they continue to normally reside at home.


                                                                                  1 SPC Regs, Sch I, para 1(1)


Example


Nasreen has no partner and lives with her son. The conditions for the award of an additional amount for
the disabled are not satisfied. Nasreen goes into a care home temporarily. An additional amount for the
severely disabled is not applicable because she continues to normally reside at home with her son.

Concept role: dwp:BenefitComponent.","text":"DMG 78270 concerns the housing-cost additional amount, not the whole Pension Credit award. It states that an additional amount for housing costs is not allowed for claimants in a care home unless their absence from the dwelling normally occupied as home is temporary. The exception does not establish payment of care-home fees. DMG 78240 allows treatment as living in the former home, with housing costs allowed, for a trial period of up to 13 weeks, subject to assessment of suitability, intention to return if unsuitable and the normally occupied part of the home not being let or sublet. This temporary-absence treatment is subject to the stated overall maximum of 52 weeks. DMG 78254–78257 set separate 52-week conditions including intention to return, no letting or subletting, a listed reason and expected duration. Permanent residence and Housing Benefit expenditure are separate exclusions. DMG 78271 defines Housing Benefit expenditure as an element for which Housing Benefit may be payable; actual payment of Housing Benefit is not stated as a condition here. Under DMG 77128, one partner entering a care home permanently is treated as no longer in the same household. Where both enter permanently, the decision maker must establish whether they remain one household on the facts. DMG 77129–77130 require reasonable independence and responsibility in running a domestic establishment; the seven factors are non-exhaustive and none is decisive alone. DMG 78089 says each may claim when household membership ends, not that an award automatically follows. Concept role: dwp:Applicability.","text":"Bounded reading of the captured Pension Credit severe-disability additional-amount rules for a claimant who has a partner. DMG 78045–78047 set distinct lower-rate branches, and 78048–78050 address the higher rate. Their benefit, residence and caring conditions must be read together. DMG 78047's patient branch concerns the other partner being unable to receive the specified benefit because of being a patient for over 28 days; its remaining conditions continue on the next page. DMG 78050 restricts the higher-rate condition when either partner is treated as receiving benefit under the partner-patient provision in 78060(2), and directs consideration of the lower rate. It does not exclude every form of treated receipt. Read the separate CA/UC actual-payment qualification in 78057, in respect of caring for the claimant or partner, and the complete treated-receipt provisions in 78060, with the dated changes in memos 02/25, 06/25 and 01/26.
